premise: In a town where every kind act makes one of your accessories jump onto the person you helped, a colourful outsider keeps helping anyway.
world_rule: In Mirrowick, every time you help someone, one accessory you wear jumps onto them. The hidden half: when the helped person says thank you, the helper's hair glows gold and a brand new copy appears on the helper.
logline: Milo arrives covered in thank-you gifts, searching for someone, and keeps helping a town that forgot kindness until one thank-you shows what the rule really means.

beats.hook: In this town, being kind is the worst thing you can do. (Shot: a hat is ripped off a helper and flies onto the person he helped.)
beats.rule: One accessory jumps per kind act; three fast examples; nobody helps anybody. Open loop: people wake up wearing tiny things nobody gave them. Milo arrives covered in accessories with a secret.
beats.conflict: Milo helps Pip and loses his red cap; it is Pip's first hat, and Milo is not sad. Mayor Tilda shows her bare hands: she helped once and lost everything. She warns him; he refuses.
escalation: The baker gets Milo's green scarf and yells at him to stay away
Milo sees the baker already wears the red scarf Milo knitted (clue)
Neighbours slam their doors as Milo walks by
By sunset Milo has nothing left but his shirt; tiny footprints lead from every door to the lighthouse
beats.reveal: In the cellar sits Lena, Milo's runaway sister. She helped everyone at night while they slept, so the rule left her ribbon, clip and red scarf on them.
beats.resolution: Pip followed Milo and says thank you; Milo's hair blazes gold and a new red cap appears. Kindness waits for thanks, which is why Milo, from a thankful home, wore so much. Pip tells the town; they thank Lena and the town turns bright.
beats.ending: The town thanks Mayor Tilda; her hair glows and a golden crown appears. Sequel hook: a locked chest 'for the one who was helped first'.
